annotations.text:
TERMINAL LEDGER - the chosen direction, built out.

IBM Plex Sans for prose, IBM Plex Mono for every number, identifier and label. Cool near-white ground, one IBM-blue accent, desaturated semantics.

Zero border-radius and no shadows anywhere. That is the identity, and it is what stops this reading as stock shadcn - literally one line in the Tailwind theme.

All of it is buildable with shadcn/ui primitives: same Radix behaviour, different token layer.

BOTH THEMES FROM ONE TOKEN SET.

The dark artboard is the light one with the token map applied - identical markup, 19 colour swaps, nothing hand-tuned. If a colour had needed special-casing, the token set would have been wrong.

Dark is NOT an inversion. Chroma is re-tuned per token so the semantics stay legible on a dark ground: the greens lift, the reds desaturate, the accent brightens.

COMPOSER shown in its BLOCKED state, deliberately.

The verifier caught 'Led a team of four engineers' - your profile records that you worked on the chatbot in a team of four, and nothing more. Participation is not leadership, so export is blocked at attempt 2 of 2.

This is the screen that makes the product defensible. A happy-path composer would demo better and prove nothing.

RUN CONSOLE - the agent actually reasoning, not a spinner.

Left: the live write_todos plan. Centre: subagent dispatches, tool calls, a rate-limited source backing off, and the interrupt where the agent hit your bulk-apply cap and stopped rather than deciding for you. Right: cost accruing per subagent, and the 75% cache-hit rate that is most of why a run costs cents.

The virtual-filesystem panel is the point: 6.4 MB of postings on disk, not in context.

MODELS AND PROVIDERS - paste a key, test, bind a tier.

Note the failing Ollama row: a connection that cannot be verified is marked and excluded from binding rather than silently failing at run time. Note also 'this stage requires vision' hiding 211 models from the application-agent picker - preflight as a UI affordance, not an error message three minutes into a browser session.

The deep tier is pinned to Anthropic while everything else runs on cheap OpenRouter models. That mix is the intended shape.

Kept for the record. B optimised for the document, C for state at a glance.

Worth lifting from C if the Job Inbox ever feels flat: its discipline of reserving one hue (violet) strictly for interaction, so semantic colour never competes with clickability.
